### Answers That Don’t Seem Like Answers
Author: Lorraine Edwards
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/encouragement/encouragement-for-today-september-1-2020.html
Passage: Exodus 14:15
Points:
- Personal struggle with fear and past pain often leads us to demand detailed, comfortable answers from God.
- Trapped by an army behind and the sea ahead, Israel was simply told to move forward into the impossible.
- Divine instruction frequently contradicts human logic, yet carries deep spiritual certainty.
- God sees what lies on the other side of our obstacles and calls us to trust His direction.

### Crying Over Answered Prayer
Author: Suzanne Eller
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/girlfriends/girlfriends-in-god-september-27-2021.html
Passage: Exodus 14:15
Points:
- Experiencing an unfolding miracle often brings unexpected challenges that can provoke fear instead of praise.
- The Israelites panicked when pursued, overlooking the miracle of freedom that was actively taking place.
- God instructed Moses to stop lamenting and command the people to move forward in faith.
- Believers must shift focus from intimidation to celebrating God's ongoing deliverance.
- Walking into answered prayer requires trusting that the Lord is present at every step.

### The Highway to the Promised Land
Author: Charles R. Swindoll
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/todays-insight-chuck-swindoll/day-by-day-apr-10-2008-11572900.html
Passage: Exodus 14:15-22
Points:
- Human ingenuity attempts to orchestrate neat outcomes, but God often orchestrates situations that leave us cornered.
- Facing an uncrossable sea strips away self-reliance and teaches us to wait on divine timing.
- Feeling trapped and overwhelmed is frequently by God's design to prepare believers for deliverance.
- Arriving at the Red Sea is essential for breaking old habits before stepping into God's promises.

### Crossing the Red Sea
Author: Ligonier Ministries
Site: Ligonier Ministries
URL: https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/crossing-the-red-sea
Passage: Exodus 14:22
Points:
- The dividing of the Red Sea reveals God's ultimate power over nature on behalf of His chosen people.
- Israel's passage through the dry sea bed typifies conversion, while the destruction of Pharaoh's army prefigures divine judgment.
- God used darkness to disorient the pursuing enemies while supernaturally illuminating Israel's path.
- Seeing God's righteous judgment and deliverance strengthens holy reverence and faith in His promises.
